screen: Quick Add, team member on a phone

markers.title: The restaurant is already known
markers.finding: The research watched reports being made during a shift. Time pressure was real but smaller than it felt: the cost people described was stepping off the floor during a rush.
markers.decision: The restaurant and its number are carried by the session, so the first screen asks nothing the system can already answer.
markers.rejected: A site picker on the first screen, which asks a casual team member for a number they have never needed to know.

markers.title: Something happened, in plain words
markers.finding: Incident type came first on the old form, with options like first aid or lost time that nobody can predict while their hand is under the cold tap.
markers.decision: Two choices, written as sentences a team member would say out loud, with the definition underneath. The industrial vocabulary never appears on the reporter's side.
markers.rejected: A dropdown of incident types, which was the field people got wrong and were corrected on from above.

markers.title: A hazard is a condition, not an event
markers.finding: The platform's hazard categories contained events rather than conditions, so a wet floor and a fall landed in the same list and the reporter had to guess which one they were looking at.
markers.decision: The hazard path is a separate entry that describes a condition that could cause harm, and it skips every question about an injury.
markers.rejected: One combined form with conditional fields, which still opens on the question the reporter cannot answer.

markers.title: The guide sits where the hesitation is
markers.finding: Team members trusted their managers and nobody described feeling afraid to report. The barrier was the form, the phone and the threshold: not knowing whether a thing counted.
markers.decision: Worked examples in the reporter's own language sit on the deciding screen, and the promise that follows them is the one the rest of the flow keeps: you will not be asked anything you cannot answer.
markers.rejected: A help link to a policy page, which moves the person away from the task at the moment they were already unsure.

markers.title: One thumb, one action
markers.finding: Restaurant visits found phone policies that differed by site and reports being made standing up, mid-shift, on a personal phone.
markers.decision: A single full-width action pinned to the bottom of every step, at a size that works with one thumb and wet hands.
markers.rejected: Next and Cancel side by side, which puts the destructive action under the thumb that is already moving.
